I have been sifting through the many discussions of polarization in the forum in order to get something into the Wiki. I can not remember what the equation is for the optimum index matching number. I somehow think it was a cosine function of n1 and n2 but I can't remember.

Here is what I have so far:

[http://www.holographyforum.org/HoloWiki ... tive_Index](http://www.holographyforum.org/HoloWiki/index.php/Refractive_Index)

[http://www.holographyforum.org/HoloWiki ... larization](http://www.holographyforum.org/HoloWiki/index.php/Polarization)

[http://www.holographyforum.org/HoloWiki ... %27s_Angle](http://www.holographyforum.org/HoloWiki/index.php/Brewster%27s_Angle)

I am sure I am forgetting lots. What is missing and/or needs to be corrected?

Thank you to Kaveh, Dave, Frank and Bob who's posts have been liberally hacked up into these pages.

posts.content_md:
No, I have that one but in a little different form.

I remember that I had posted that it seemed to me that if we had glass at 1.5 and gelatin at 1.35 then we would want (1.5+1.35)/2 as an ideal index match. Someone corrected me and the actual value was a little higher than my simple reasoning would suggest.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
It's the geometric mean - sqrt(n0n1)

See [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_coating](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_coating)

about halfway down

Also, "In order to obtain a desired value of the refractive index, two different liquids can be mixed, giving an index calculated according to 

P1/100 = (nm - n2) / (n1 - n2)

where P1 denotes the volume percent of component 1, n1 is the index of component 1, n2 that of component 2, and nm that of the mixture. This expression is approximate as it assumes volume additivity...."

from Bjelkhagen, Silver Halide Recording Materials, p. 239
